meta.title: Alexandre Morel — International journalist, documentary & communications
meta.description: International journalist covering crisis zones: field investigation, documentary production and journalism training — for ARTE, France 24, Al Jazeera, France 5 and Public Sénat, across Africa, the Middle East, Asia and the Balkans.

hero.subtitle: I explore international realities through reporting, documentary production and editorial work.
hero.complement: I work with media, producers and organisations on projects that require a deep understanding of the field, of local contexts and of human stakes.
hero.approach: My approach combines international experience, listening, adaptability and editorial rigour to turn complex realities into stories that are accessible, documented and human.

intro.title: Understanding the field before telling the story.
intro.p1: For more than twenty years I have been covering crisis zones and sensitive contexts — in Africa, the Middle East, Asia and the Balkans — for ARTE, France 24, Al Jazeera, France 5 and Public Sénat.
intro.p2: An event is never reduced to what is immediately visible: there is a context, people, trajectories and realities that give information its full depth.
intro.p3: My work is to go out and meet these realities, to understand what shapes them and to build narratives that allow audiences to grasp the issues — from breaking-news reporting to long-form documentary.
intro.p4: This approach rests on field investigation, listening, source protection and a constant attention to the accuracy of information.

approach.title: A proven method, step by step.
approach.lede: Twenty years of fieldwork in sensitive zones — Africa, the Middle East, Asia, the Balkans — have forged a simple, demanding method, common to all my projects, from news reporting to documentary.

steps.title: Field listening
steps.desc: Before writing or filming, I meet the people who live the story. On the ground, face to face — listening that reveals what no press release ever will.

steps.title: Context understanding
steps.desc: Every fact belongs to a history, an economy, a culture. I connect those threads so each piece of information sits within the reality that shapes it — ruling out misreading from the start.

steps.title: Story building
steps.desc: From that raw material rises a clear architecture: a story designed for its audience, compelling without ever trading nuance for jargon.

steps.title: Rigorous delivery
steps.desc: Source verification, balance of perspectives, precision of language: the essential, delivered on time, equal to the stakes — and defensible under scrutiny.

steps.title: Craft transmission
steps.desc: Masterclasses, newsroom training, team mentoring: from the Faculty of Journalism of Tunis to the newsrooms of Afghanistan and Cambodia, I share the methods and reflexes that make journalists autonomous — investigation, media ethics, fake news, source protection.

expertise.title: Complex subjects. Accessible stories.
expertise.lede: Twenty years of fieldwork across four complementary areas of practice — each domain opens onto a selection of works and collaborations.

productions.intro2: An encounter, an event, a context or a question that deserves to be explored beyond the obvious.
productions.intro3: From Afghanistan to Ukraine, from Libya to Tunisia: a selection of documentaries and reports — recognised with two Étoiles de la Scam and a Prix Jeunes FIGRA — illustrating my field approach and the attention paid to the people at the heart of each story.

publications.intro1: Some questions call for more than an immediate reaction.
publications.intro2: They require perspective, a careful reading of the facts and an understanding of contexts.

meta.title: About
meta.description: International journalist and media consultant specialising in crisis zones: more than 20 years of field investigation, documentary production and journalism training in Africa, the Middle East, Asia and the Balkans.

hero.title: International experience in the service of accurate, documented storytelling.
hero.p1: An international journalist and media consultant, I specialise in crisis zones: more than twenty years of field investigation, documentary production and journalism training in Africa, the Middle East, Asia and the Balkans.
hero.p2: A correspondent for ARTE, France 24, Al Jazeera, France 5, Public Sénat and Radio France, my career was built through contact with different cultures and contexts — from Kabul to Cairo, from Tunis to Athens — with collaborations for Libération, Le Temps and L'Express.
hero.p3: These experiences shaped a specific expertise: field reporting, international journalist networks, source protection and the passing on of skills in sensitive environments.

journey.title: From Kabul to the Balkans: twenty years of postings.
journey.p1: The journey begins with transmission: taking part in the creation of the daily newspaper Cambodge Soir and training Cambodian journalists, then training camerawomen and Afghan journalists for the Aïna association in Kabul — years of journeys across Asia, Africa and the Arab world.
journey.p2: Then came the war postings: Afghanistan and Pakistan for ARTE, Radio France and France 24, with collaborations for Libération, Le Temps and L'Express — TV, radio and print coverage, producing content in war zones and field coordination in high-risk contexts.
journey.p3: Then post-Arab Spring Tunisia for ARTE, Egypt and Libya for ARTE and France 24 — international reports demanding adaptation, discretion and the handling of sensitive sources, built on a local network of institutional contacts, journalists and field actors established over the years.
journey.p4: From Greece and the Balkans, I now produce reports and geopolitical analyses for ARTE — with continuous coverage of Greek and Balkan affairs and of the Ukrainian conflict since 2022. A career marked by two Étoiles de la Scam and a Prix Jeunes FIGRA.

vision.title: Telling without oversimplifying. Understanding without prejudging.
vision.p1: A master's degree in philosophy, training as a video journalist at the CFPJ, war-zone journalism training: I regard journalism as a craft of understanding as much as of transmission.
vision.p2: It is not only about reporting facts, but giving them a context, making the relevant perspectives heard and helping audiences better grasp the issues at stake.
vision.p3: Source protection, media ethics and the fight against fake news are not options: they are the very conditions of the craft.

beyond.title: An experience that can serve other projects.
beyond.p1: As a media consultant and trainer, I support newsrooms, universities and organisations: editorial project supervision, field mentoring, pedagogical structuring — from the Faculty of Journalism of Tunis, where I teach investigation, media ethics, fake news, source protection and social networks, to African capitals.
beyond.p2: Co-founder of the North African Correspondent Club (NAFCC), dedicated to the defence of press freedom, I also develop media projects and their financing: international project coordination, intercultural communication, fundraising — as in 2025, with the assessment of journalistic needs across several African capitals for the Afrikibaaru2 programme (CFI).
beyond.p3: Understanding a context, identifying the stakes of a message and building a suitable narrative: my approach always begins with listening to the need and understanding the objectives.

meta.description: Field reports and investigations in sensitive zones: correspondent in Afghanistan, Pakistan, Tunisia, Egypt, Libya and the Balkans for ARTE, France 24, Radio France, Libération, Le Temps and L'Express.

hero.title: Understanding international realities. Telling them with accuracy.
hero.p1: International journalism demands particular attention to contexts, people and the dynamics that shape events — especially in crisis zones, where information itself is a stake of power.
hero.p2: From Kabul to Cairo and from Athens to Tunis, my work as a correspondent is to document these realities, gather the relevant perspectives and build narratives that make the issues accessible — on television, on radio and in print.

approach.title: Going into the field to understand what is at stake.
approach.p1: Information cannot be fully understood without taking its environment into account.
approach.p2: Covering a sensitive zone requires rigorous preparation: understanding the actors and the balances, securing and protecting one's sources, working discreetly — gestures that are learned and passed on.
approach.p3: This approach makes it possible to put facts back into context, to better grasp geopolitical and societal issues, and to build a narrative faithful to the documented reality.

meta.title: Documentary
meta.description: Documentary narratives with a strong human dimension: films broadcast by ARTE, France 5, Al Jazeera and Public Sénat — recognised with two Étoiles de la Scam and a Prix Jeunes FIGRA.

hero.title: Giving a place to human stories.
hero.p1: Documentary offers the time needed to understand a reality, to meet the people who live it and to explore its many dimensions.
hero.p2: My approach is to build narratives combining an understanding of the field, attention to people and narrative rigour — from the 90-minute feature to the four-part documentary series.

approach.title: Understanding a story before telling it.
approach.p1: Every documentary project has its own context, its own interlocutors and its own stakes.
approach.p2: The work begins with a thorough understanding of the subject, then continues with gathering the elements needed to build the narrative — video capture (Premiere Pro, Filmic Pro), audio editing (Audacity), writing and editorial production.
approach.p3: The goal is to give shape to that material without ever losing sight of the subject's reality, or of the responsibility towards the people encountered.

hero.title: Understanding the news beyond the events.
hero.p1: International events only take on their full meaning through the contexts that shape them.
hero.p2: Through my articles, analyses and journalistic features, I explore international realities, the dynamics that run through them and the human stories that deserve to be told.
hero.p3: My goal: to bring elements of understanding, put the news into perspective and offer a documented take on the issues shaping our world.

intro.title: Taking the time to understand.
intro.p1: Information travels fast. Understanding sometimes requires more distance.
intro.p2: Some questions call for going beyond the immediate event, placing the facts back in their context and taking different perspectives into account.
intro.p3: My publications are part of that approach.
intro.p4: Each article is an opportunity to explore a subject, shed light on its stakes and give readers elements to better understand international realities.

meta.description: Understanding the stakes, building messages that make sense: editorial support nourished by twenty years of international journalism — intercultural communication, media projects and fundraising.

hero.title: Understanding the stakes. Building messages that make sense.
hero.p1: An effective message must be clear, coherent and adapted to its context.
hero.p2: My experience as an international correspondent nourishes a communication approach attentive to the understanding of stakes, to the quality of messages and to the relationship with audiences — including intercultural ones.

approach.title: Clarity begins with understanding.
approach.p1: Before building a message, it is essential to understand the situation, the objectives and the audiences it addresses.
approach.p2: This approach makes it possible to define a suitable editorial strategy, structure the essential information and build more coherent communication — drawing on intercultural communication, the coordination of international media projects and project development (fundraising).

meta.title: Training & Knowledge Transfer
meta.description: Training journalists in sensitive contexts: investigation, media ethics, fake news, source protection. Interventions across Africa, the Middle East and Asia — in French and English.

hero.title: Passing on experience. Improving practice.
hero.p1: From the creation of the daily newspaper Cambodge Soir to the Faculty of Journalism of Tunis, transmission runs through the whole journey: training local journalists in Cambodia, Afghanistan, Pakistan, Tunisia and Egypt.
hero.p2: My approach favours exchange, concrete examples and adaptation to participants' needs: investigation, media ethics, fake news, source protection and social networks.

interventions.p1: Would you like to organise a training course, mentoring or a professional intervention — in a newsroom, at a university or within an international programme?
interventions.p2: I intervene in French and English, on site and remotely: editorial project supervision, field mentoring, pedagogical structuring.
interventions.p3: A recent mission (2025): assessing the journalistic needs of several African capitals for the Afrikibaaru2 programme (CFI).
